JURY_SERVICE.HEADING: How jury service works
JURY_SERVICE.INTRO: What jury service is and who can be called.

WHAT_IS_JURY_SERVICE.TITLE: What is jury service?
WHAT_IS_JURY_SERVICE.CONTENT: Jury service is an important public duty. You and usually 11 other people will form a jury. Together, you’ll decide the result of a criminal trial in the Crown court.

WHO_CAN_BE_CALLED.TITLE: Who can be called for jury service?
WHO_CAN_BE_CALLED.CONTENT_1: Every adult aged 18 to 75 years that lives in the UK can be picked at random for jury service from the electoral roll.
WHO_CAN_BE_CALLED.CONTENT_2: If you are going to be under 18 or over 76 on the first day of your jury service, you will be unable to serve but you must still reply to your summons.

INFORMATION.TITLE: Information for employees and self-employed jurors
INFORMATION.CONTENT_1: Your employer has to let you do jury service – it’s the law, but they can ask you to apply to change the dates to a more convenient time (you can only do this once). See the information about asking to change your dates or be excused, or check [link] for more details.
INFORMATION.CONTENT_2: Your employer can choose whether or not to pay you during your service. If they do not pay you, you can claim for loss of earnings from the court, subject to a daily maximum. If you are self-employed, you have the right to claim the same allowances as if you were an employee.
INFORMATION.CONTENT_3: Check the information in the ‘claiming expenses’ section or at [link] for more details.

CHANGE_DATES.HEADING: Asking to change your dates or to be excused
CHANGE_DATES.INTRO: When you respond to your summons, you can ask to change your dates or to be excused from your jury service.

CHANGING_YOUR_DATES.TITLE: Changing your dates
CHANGING_YOUR_DATES.CONTENT_1: You can only change the dates of your service once and you'll need to give us a reason. You will be asked to provide some alternative dates within 12 months when you could serve.

BEING_EXCUSED.TITLE: Being excused
BEING_EXCUSED.CONTENT_1: Excusals are only granted in exceptional circumstances when you cannot serve at any time in the following 12 months.
BEING_EXCUSED.CONTENT_2: You may be asked to provide evidence, but you won't need to include this when you respond. We'll contact you and give you time to gather anything we need.
BEING_EXCUSED.CONTENT_3: If you need more information, please see [link].

ELIGIBILITY.HEADING: Who is eligible to serve on a jury?
ELIGIBILITY.INTRO: As part of your response, you'll be asked questions to help us decide whether you can do jury service.

QUALIFY.TITLE: You qualify for jury service if
QUALIFY.BULLET_1: you will be at least 18 years old, and under 76 years old, on the day that you start your jury service
QUALIFY.BULLET_2: you are registered as a parliamentary or local government elector
QUALIFY.BULLET_3: you have lived in the United Kingdom, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man for any period of at least five years since you were 13 years old

MENTAL_DISORDERS.TITLE: Mental disorders
MENTAL_DISORDERS.CONTENT_1: Under the Mental Health Act 1983, some people cannot do jury service.
MENTAL_DISORDERS.CONTENT_2: If you are detained, sometimes called being sectioned, in hospital, under a guardianship order or under a community treatment order because of a mental disorder, you cannot be on a jury.
MENTAL_DISORDERS.CONTENT_3: If you suffer from a mental disorder, including depression and anxiety, but you are not being detained, looked after or treated under the Mental Health Act, you can still be on a jury.

MENTAL_CAPACITY.TITLE: Mental capacity
MENTAL_CAPACITY.CONTENT_1: If you lack the mental capacity to serve as a juror, you cannot be on a jury. Mental capacity means being able to make a decision for yourself.
MENTAL_CAPACITY.CONTENT_2: To be on a jury, a person must be able to understand, remember, weigh up and communicate information relating to a decision.
MENTAL_CAPACITY.CONTENT_3: If you are not sure if you can do jury service because of a mental disorder or lack of mental capacity, you can phone us on 0300 456 1024 for advice.

BAIL.TITLE: Bail
BAIL.CONTENT_1: If you are on bail in criminal proceedings, you cannot do jury service.

CONVICTIONS.TITLE: Convictions
CONVICTIONS.CONTENT_1: You can do jury service if you have points on your driving licence, speeding fines or have been to a speed awareness course, as long as you have not received one of the sentences below.
CONVICTIONS.CONTENT_2: You cannot do jury service if you have ever had a sentence of imprisonment for life, detention for life, custody for life, imprisonment for public protection, detention for public protection, an extended sentence, or a term of imprisonment or detention of five years or more.
CONVICTIONS.CONTENT_3: You cannot do jury service if, in the last 10 years, you have served any part of a sentence of imprisonment or detention, received a suspended sentence, or had a community order in England and Wales.
CONVICTIONS.CONTENT_4: You also cannot do jury service if in the last 10 years you have had any similar order under the law of Scotland, Northern Ireland, Isle of Man, any of the Channel Islands, or a community or overseas community order under the Armed Forces Act 2006.
